chapter: Pianists, Basie, Lil Armstrong and closing
title: Chicago pianists: Earl Hines, Cassino Simpson and Art Tatum
summary: Hines dominated Chicago piano, Cassino Simpson rivalled him, and Art Tatum scared everyone at breakfast dances.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: No, no. And then -- no, because, see, during those days Earl Hines really had the influence of taking over this town. As a piano player he had really taken it over, and he --
Right, right, right. And then, see, then they had another guy here who was a tremendous piano player. He went to the crazy house, though, Cassino Simpson. Are you familiar with --
I've heard records -- he played similarly to Earl.

Right, right, right, right, and he was one of the competitors for Earl at that particular time. So -- locally, and then later on when Art Tatum came here in the '30s down to the Three Deuces, so that --

Oh, it scared everybody. And then, the same breakfast dances, they would tie up every once in a while, and at one of the breakfast dances, Art would be there and Earl would be there. So everybody wanted to hear the two of them play, but very seldom did they play from each other. Art would play at the drop of a hat.
